## Overview

 

This document sets out the timetable, application requirements, and task checklist to prepare Blaise Kelly for the White Rose Doctoral Training Partnership (WRDTP) studentship competition for entry in October 2027.

 

The primary funding route is the Advanced Quantitative Methods (AQM) Award, with parallel eligibility for the Advanced Data Analytics (ADA) Award and standard Pathway Awards.

 

## Key Dates and Timetable

 

* **Week beginning 28 September 2026**: Academic interview and research discussion with prospective supervisors.

* **Wednesday 30 September 2026 (10:00 to 11:00)**: WRDTP Collaborative Awards briefing session for academic supervisors.

* **Wednesday 7 October 2026 (11:00 to 12:00)**: WRDTP staff briefing session on Pathway, AQM, and ADA awards.

* **Thursday 8 October 2026 (17:30 to 18:30)**: WRDTP applicant briefing session for prospective students.

* **October to November 2026**: Formal application submission via the University of Leeds research degrees portal.

* **October to December 2026**: Iterative drafting of proposal text in `index.qmd` and matching Word application fields.

* **December 2026 to early January 2027**: Faculty internal review and shortlisting at the University of Leeds.

* **Wednesday 20 January 2027 (17:00 UK time)**: Strict deadline for applicants to submit their completed studentship application form to the University of Leeds.

* **Wednesday 24 February 2027**: Deadline for the University of Leeds to submit official candidate nominations to the WRDTP.

* **April to May 2027**: WRDTP funding outcomes announced.

* **October 2027**: PhD start date.

 

## Application Form Access and Locations

 

The application process involves two distinct forms: the Student Application Form and the Supervisor Nomination Form.

 

### 1. Student Application Form

 

* Only the information provided by the applicant in this form attracts marks.

* The official preview version is hosted on Google Docs: [WRDTP Application Form Preview](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fJV3lGWAQw_jOVOl38W33In_yJm9l_27tZb0_Jeh_DE/edit?usp=drive_link).

* Access to the Google Doc requires an institutional login.

* The University of Leeds Graduate School Office will also distribute an editable Microsoft Word version directly to applicants who apply via the Leeds study portal.

* Applicants must not submit directly to the WRDTP. All submissions go through the University of Leeds Graduate School.

 

### 2. Supervisor Nomination Form

 

* This form is completed by the supervisory team and institutional leads.

* The official preview is available on Google Docs: [WRDTP Nomination Form Preview](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1F92uKQdXjRduprlmji7ayaHc9sLUjXqXeryBUY2IN_8/edit?usp=drive_link).

* Nominating universities submit final nominations using an online Google Form in February 2027.

* Per University of Leeds best practice, supervisors should draft all responses in an offline Word document before final submission.

 

### 3. University Study Application

 

* In addition to the scholarship form, Blaise must submit a formal application for a PhD place through the University of Leeds application portal: [Applying for research degrees at Leeds](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/research-applying/doc/applying-research-degrees).

* Candidates must hold an offer of study to be eligible for nomination.

 

## Structure of the Application Form

 

* **Section 1: Applicant Details and Programme Selection**: Selection of award type (Pathway, AQM, ADA) and award duration (3.5 years, 3.75 years with integrated PGCert, or 4.5 years with MA Social Research).

* **Section 2: About Your Project (Double-weighted: 10 marks out of 20)**: Research questions, background, methodology, feasibility, ethics, positionality, and APA references. Applicants for AQM and ADA must complete additional dedicated boxes detailing their advanced quantitative methods and data analytics.

* **Section 3: Project Fit with WRDTP Core Priorities (5 marks out of 20)**: Alignment with thematic interdisciplinary pathways and planned pathways to societal and economic impact.

* **Section 4: Applicant Motivation and Potential (5 marks out of 20)**: Personal and professional motivation, research potential, and evidence of transferable skills.

* **Section 5: Stuart Hall Foundation Statement**: Optional statement for eligible Black British applicants.

* **Section 6: Applicant Declarations**: Confirmation of eligibility and accuracy.

* **Section 7: Statement on the Use of Artificial Intelligence**: Mandatory disclosure and description of any AI tools used during proposal preparation.
